claims.claim: Some high-utilization factories may value verified lifecycle energy cost more than the lowest purchase price.
A combined equipment and service offer could create a more defensible difference than a specification-only message.

counter_evidence: Customers may prioritize purchase price or procurement rules over lifecycle cost.
Energy savings may depend more on factory operations and maintenance discipline than supplier equipment.
Competitors may copy audits and service bundles quickly.
Service intensity may erode margins if route density is low.
unknowns: Actual segment size and willingness to pay.
Measured energy savings under matched operating conditions.
Service cost per installed unit and renewal rate.
Competitor proof and customer switching costs.
